title: Equations Using Identities
subject: mathematics

theory.introduction: More complicated trigonometric equations can be transformed into solvable forms using identities already learned.

content.text: Choose an identity that reduces the number of different trigonometric functions or creates a familiar algebraic form.
Pythagorean, reciprocal, double-angle, and sum-and-difference identities can transform complicated equations.

formulas.name: Pythagorean Identity
formulas.explanation: Useful for converting between sine and cosine.

formulas.name: Double-Angle Identity
formulas.explanation: Can convert a double-angle expression into a squared trigonometric function.

examples.question: Solve 1 − 2sin²(x) = 0 for 0 ≤ x < 2π.
examples.solution: Rearrange to sin²(x) = 1/2. Therefore sin(x) = ±√2/2. The four solutions are π/4, 3π/4, 5π/4, and 7π/4.

key_ideas: Return to a basic trigonometric equation whenever possible.
misconceptions: Using an identity without considering whether it simplifies the equation.
Assuming every identity makes an equation easier.
